summary: Bare rock in Chatham Sound, 15 km south of Prince Rupert: a beacon moved here in 1908, a lighthouse first lit in 1913, burned in 1946, a steel tower since 1949.

structures.note: Square tower with an octagonal lantern room, built into the corner of a two-storey dwelling on a concrete pier (LighthouseFriends); destroyed by fire in 1946 (LighthouseFriends, Rowlett).
Square, cylindrical steel skeletal tower on the fog-signal building; present light (Rowlett). The Coast Guard list calls it a square skeleton tower.

access.note: Site and tower closed (Rowlett). LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower closed. Reached only by boat.

events.note: Automatic acetylene beacon placed on Green Top Island.
Automatic acetylene beacon moved from Green Top Island to Holland Rock, May 1908 (Department report; LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
Work begins on a formal lighthouse for the rock; contract for $13,500 to J.H. Hilditch (LighthouseFriends).
Two-storey dwelling with a square tower on a concrete pier (Rowlett; LighthouseFriends).
Keeper James E. Gibson first exhibited the fixed white light (LighthouseFriends).
In September an overheated cook stove set fire to the lighthouse; the keeper fled the rock in the station skiff. Rubble and the brick chimney remained.
White skeletal steel tower on the concrete pier, and a fog-alarm building with two compressors and a diaphone horn (LighthouseFriends; Rowlett).
Experimental microwave remote control of the fog alarm from Barrett Rock, about 8 km (4.9 miles) away.
Coast Guard proposed a new concrete helicopter pad after the wooden pad collapsed (federal assessment record).

corrections.why: The record's 1908 date (from Rowlett's 'station established') is the year the automatic beacon was moved to the rock. The lighthouse with its square tower was first lit in 1913, per LighthouseFriends and Rowlett. Reviewed by a human; not applied.
The 1908 structure in the record (Wikidata) was the beacon, not a tower. The first tower on the rock was built in 1913, and the present 6 m steel skeleton tower came in 1949.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Two dates for the first mark on the rock. 1908 is the automatic acetylene beacon moved from Green Top Island (Department report for fiscal 1908-09). 1913 is the first lighthouse, built after work began in 1912.

The record's 'lost' belongs to the 1913 lighthouse, which the fire of 1946 destroyed. The 'standing' structure is the 1949 steel skeleton tower on the fog-signal building, which the Coast Guard list and Rowlett describe.

notes_for_editor:
Sources. LighthouseFriends (3) is a copyrighted community site, used for facts only, paraphrased, with one-line quotes; its 1955 Electronics article is second-hand. Rowlett (4) is a directory. The federal assessment (5) is a government project record, not a history.

Disagreements left open in the story: (a) Access. Rowlett says 'Site and tower closed'; LighthouseFriends says 'Grounds open, tower closed'. The story reports both and invites no landing. (b) Distance from Prince Rupert: Rowlett 15 km, the 2020 assessment 16 km. (c) Focal height: the Coast Guard gives 9.1 m, Rowlett gives a 7 m focal plane. The Coast Guard figure is used. (d) Naming: LighthouseFriends says Captain Pender named the rock in 1867 after Holland. A search snippet from a place-name book (KnowBC) gives a different account, linking Holland to HMS Malacca. I did not read that page in full, so the story gives only LighthouseFriends' version.

OCR columns not used. The 1913 contract table (1914v48, scan 60 and the nearby pages) has 'J. Hilditch' and a 'combined dwelling, fog alarm and light house on concrete pier' row. Those are split across columns, so I did not match them to Holland Rock. The 1913-14 'Statement of lightstations and names of lightkeepers' (scan 78-79) is also split: names, months and dates sit in separate columns, so no keeper date comes from it. A checker should read the page image for any keeper date.

Name-only coincidence, not linked: a Stanley Fredrick Lawrence is listed here for 1920-1921, and a Stanley F. Lawrence at Cape St. James for 1921-1931. No source connects them.

No women keepers are named in the sources read. The pet cat in the 1946 escape comes only from LighthouseFriends.

Chronicling America searches for 'Holland Rock' returned nothing relevant. The Canadian Coast Guard's 2020 helipad project is a proposal; I found no record that it was completed.

Lens and current light-source details are not in the sources read.
